messages:
alice: Heads up — saw a big p95 spike around 10:12 UTC during the onboarding workflow. Latency jumped ~3x for about 6m. Autoscaler added 4 nodes but most came up cold; warm pool had been evicted earlier.
ben: yup, saw it too. infra-bot shows host evictions due to OOM from tenant 'video-transcode' at 10:10. Warm-pool count dropped 8 -> 2.
carol: profiler (short) from one affected runtime:
```
wall_time: 00:00:04.12
attention_kernel_ms: 2200
matmul_generic_ms: 1800
quantized_kernel_ms: 150
kernel_selector: fallback -> generic_matmul
batching_latency_ms: 420
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.38
```
carol: note the kernel_selector flipped to the generic kernel for the sequence distribution in this window — kernel warmups/artefacts probably missing on the new nodes.
maya: KV cache metrics align: cache miss rate jumped 2% -> 38% at 10:11, active prefixes got invalidated when we drained/evicted GPUs. That explains token amplification.
alice: @ben can you paste autoscaler/events around 10:08-10:15? wondering if provisioning policy picked a different accel family.
ben: autoscaler events: 
```
10:07:50 decision: scale_up +4
10:08:05 provisioning: created instances: gpu:ampere-spot x4
10:09:40 kube: nodes registered
10:10:20 warm_pool reconcile: evict 6 nodes due to memory_pressure from pod video-transcode
```
ben: warm pool didn't have matching accelerator type (was A100 reserved) so new ampere-spot instances weren't eligible as warm-pool members -> they came up cold. Provisioning delay ~90s.
carol: putting it together: noisy neighbor consumer caused warm-pool eviction -> autoscaler launched wrong instance family (spot) -> runtime couldn't load quantized/optimized kernels (cache miss & kernel_selector fallback) -> batching heuristics increased in-flight batches because cold nodes had different throughput characteristics -> KV cache cold -> p95 spike.
maya: temporary mitigations applied at 10:23: increased warm_pool_ttl to 900s, set warm_pool_affinity to prefer matching accelerator_family, bumped autoscaler cooldown to 120s, enabled kernel preload on node-init (preload list includes quantized kernels and attention kernels).
ben: config patch we pushed (diff):
```yaml
autoscaler:
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  preferred_accelerator_family: A100
warm_pool:
  ttl_seconds: 900
  min_available: 4
node_init:
  kernel_preload: ["attn_opt_v2", "matmul_quant", "kv_cache_shard"]
```
infra-bot: Patch infra/patches/1729 applied to prod at 10:25 UTC :rocket: (CI passed, no rollback)
deploy-bot: rolled-back:false, rollout:gradual 100%
alice: metrics look back to normal at 10:30 — p95 returned to baseline. Adding a short postmortem and follow-up tasks: 1) make warm-pool eviction alerts more visible, 2) add kernel_preload as a default for warm nodes, 3) add autoscaler policy to prefer warm-compatible instance types, 4) add an early-warning for KV cache miss surges.
carol: will add a perf regression test that simulates warm-pool loss + noisy memory pressure to catch kernel_selector fallbacks in CI.
maya: leaving monitoring on for 24h, will post summary tomorrow. :thumbsup:
